- Hotel: Bairro Alto Hotel, Praça Luís de Camões 2, 1200-243 Lisboa (breakfast included)

---

## 2. DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS
Required language (per content agreement + Partnership Standards & Disclosure Policy):
> "This trip was hosted by Visit Lisbon in partnership with Nina Caldwell Media. All opinions are my own."

Placement rules:
- Blog posts: disclosure at TOP, before body text
- Instagram captions: first line, not buried after line breaks
- Newsletter: first sentence of the dedicated section
- Story frames: frame #1 of the delivered set

FTC note: 'Clear and conspicuous' standard applies to newsletter footers too — do not rely on footer-only disclosure for email.

|---|---|---|

Revised shot list priority locations: Alfama & Miradouro da Graça, Belém, LX Factory, Mouraria, Sintra & Cascais, Bairro Alto & Chiado.

title: Roam & Earn Early-Bird Decision — Working Notes (2026-02-24)
content:
Working notes from the Feb 24 budget review block (EVT-323).

## The Question
Should I commit to Roam & Earn Phase 1 at the early-bird rate ($240) before the Feb 27 deadline, or wait for the Wanderluxe installment to clear?

## Key Numbers
- Current confirmed Q2 sponsorship revenue: $1,050
- Current confirmed affiliate budget cap (20%): $210
- Wanderluxe Installment #1 pending: $450 (due March 5, clears March 3–5)
- Post-installment cap: $300
- Phase 1 early-bird: $240 (non-refundable, deadline Feb 27)
- Phase 1 standard: $300 (available from March 1)
- Price delta: $60

## The Problem
The installment clears AFTER the early-bird deadline. Committing now at $240 against a $210 cap = $30 over policy. Non-refundable.

## Risk Math
- Probability installment clears before Feb 27: ~15% (Wanderluxe confirmed March 1 batch processing)
- Expected overspend if I commit now: ~85% × $30 = ~$25.50
- Opportunity cost of waiting: $60 (certain)

On pure expected value, waiting costs more ($60 certain vs. ~$25.50 expected). BUT — the overspend isn't really probabilistic here. Wanderluxe literally told me they process on March 1. The installment will NOT clear before Feb 27. It's near-certain, not 85%.

## Decision
HOLD. The $60 opportunity cost is real and it stings, but committing $240 against a $210 cap when I know the installment won't clear in time is a policy violation, not a calculated risk. The policy exists for a reason — I've had months where expected income didn't materialize.

Plan: Reply to Sophie today, explain I'm holding pending a payment clearance, ask if she can informally hold a standard-rate slot until March 5. Worst case I pay $300 instead of $240. That's fine.

## Next Steps
- Reply to Sophie (MSG-5071) — today
- Watch for Wanderluxe clearance week of March 3
- Commit Phase 1 at $300 once confirmed
- Update NPAG-33 and WB-6
